backbone: Prove the BSD formula prime by prime: integral Selmer/determinant comparisons, Heegner heights and theta congruences give matching divisibilities of the leading term and Sha.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:single} proves the single-curve inequality, and Section~\ref{sec:pair} constructs the integral pair quotients.

backbone: Assume a spectral component is missed; lifting to characteristic zero gives a nonzero sheaf with vanishing nearby cycles, which Hecke transversality and slicing show impossible.
quote: A missing spectral component leads to a contradiction as follows.

backbone: Build a sieve weight favouring a prime in (m,m+h] and few primes after; second-moment bounds plus bounded multiplicity convert weighted mass into many long gaps.
quote: One second-moment estimate detects the first prime; a separate second-moment estimate converts the resulting weighted mass into a positive proportion of ordinary integer starts.

backbone: If K_X+(n+1)L fails generation at x, a minimizing valuation exists; tangential first variation plus Brunn-Minkowski excludes positive-dimensional centers, then vanishing lifts a section, contradiction.
quote: A uniform restriction-space estimate and Brunn--Minkowski give a contradictory lower bound.

backbone: Extremal holomorphic discs and Hessian estimates give bounded canonical potentials (nefness); Monge-Ampere volume bounds give positive top self-intersection, hence bigness, projectivity and ampleness.
quote: Passing to the limit in cohomology as $t\downarrow0$ proves $\int_X c_1(K_X)^n>0$.

backbone: Constancy of a resolution invariant via semistable log models and Euler characteristics yields a simultaneous resolution; transport is extended to ambient right-trivialization, with log-canonical cases separate.
quote: Our argument instead obtains transport from a resolved zero family and extends it to the ambient function levels.

backbone: Combine cited packet-propagation and Kakeya maximal theorems through a density conversion to weighted tubes, sparse-ball epsilon removal and multiscale covering, then transfer graphs to general surfaces.
quote: The remainder of the proof gives the density conversion, the estimates for rough \(L^3\) graph data, and the passage to general surfaces.

backbone: Randomly construct cut families on a column model of the planar graph by multiscale local updates; every outcome gives the upper bound, random changes give the lower bound.
quote: We construct two families of measurable label sets, denoted by $\mathcal A_v$ and $\mathcal B_v$ at a point $v$.

backbone: Prove the sharp entropy lower bound for log-concave densities via Gaussian Brenier transport and a chaos decomposition with certified scalar estimates, then deduce the simplex inequality.
quote: The proof proceeds through differential entropy.

backbone: Give an explicit FPRAS: marked-edge enlarged graphs with vertex scaling, a rapidly mixing product chain via a two-coordinate energy inequality, and an annealing schedule converting samples to counts.

backbone: Suppose a small PSD factorization; Fourier smoothing of matrix squares turns it into low-degree sums of squares, which a parity/expander separating functional contradicts.
quote: This is the step that lets the separating functional contradict the factorization.

backbone: Explicit randomized algorithm: isolate a target, estimate a modular Fourier checksum by filtered frequency matching, extract all aliases and subtract their phases; low-deficiency inputs handled by preliminary search.
quote: We estimate the modular sum and subtract the phases of a complete list of aliases.

backbone: Show every L2 eigenfunction of the flow is constant: angular-Fourier energy estimates give transverse rigidity, then holonomy at the irrational vertex forces constancy.
quote: Expand a bounded eigenfunction on the double in angular Fourier modes.

backbone: A deterministic reduction turns suitable line data in a prime plane into a hypergraph with cover number q+1; such data exist with high probability under random deletion and selection.
quote: Under uniform deletion of a fixed number of lines per direction, with probability tending to one every small core cover also covers almost all of the whole plane.

backbone: Given a fractional cover, suppose F is not p-small; a multiscale random-colouring selector estimate with minimum-fragment covers then produces a cheap integral cover, contradiction.
quote: Suppose, for a contradiction, that $\mathcal F$ is not $p$-small.

backbone: Exhibit an explicit Maker strategy from a 722-line certificate of conditional winning positions combined recursively, verified by an executable checker to win within 21 moves.
quote: there is one globally legal Maker policy that completes an allowed copy of $S$ within at most $21$ actual Maker claims against every legal continuation of Breaker.

backbone: Construct an explicit triangular algebra from a symmetric algebra, two twisted bimodules and a degree-three class; stable Hom computations show the nonprojective module has vanishing self-extensions.
quote: We construct a finite-dimensional algebra $\Lambda$ over $k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)$ and a finite-dimensional nonprojective left module $Z$ such that $\Ext^i_\Lambda(Z,Z)=\Ext^i_\Lambda(Z,\Lambda)=0$ for every $i>0$.

backbone: Tightness and subsequential couplings, local word/chart laws, and a comparison-rigidity argument identify the limit metric with LQG up to a deterministic constant, normalized away; q>4 gives CRT separately.
quote: From every subsequence of sizes tending to infinity there is a further subsequence and a representation coupling on which the following properties hold almost surely, simultaneously.

backbone: Crossing estimates give tightness of interfaces; a discrete boundary observable built from transfer-matrix/row algebra identifies the Loewner driver of every subsequential limit as SLE_kappa.
quote: The proof combines finite connection comparisons below one, localization in irregular tiled disks, and a boundary observable that determines the limiting Loewner driver.

backbone: Efron-Stein concentration of a capped last satisfiable index plus an interpolation comparison across system sizes makes the normalized centers converge, defining the threshold as a limit.
quote: Finally, errors that are summable over geometrically increasing sizes cannot produce macroscopic drift.

backbone: Take the explicit periodic Steinberg group St_12(R) over a finitely presented matrix-nil graded algebra; phases of long words and homological stability let degree truncations detect all elements.
quote: We construct an infinite group with an ordinary finite presentation in which every element has finite order, answering the finitely presented Burnside question negatively.

backbone: Construct an amalgam of F_100 with a direct product; height extensions have cost near one, while compression, Bernoulli transfer and a planar rank bound keep Bernoulli cost above one.
quote: We construct a finitely generated group with two essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions of different costs.

backbone: Random-interchange loop representation with pinned returns; a pin bootstrap and long-return bounds reduce the magnetization deficit to random-walk return probabilities whose sum yields the Bloch coefficient.
quote: Our proof therefore estimates the observable through a representation that remains uniform under arbitrary extra up-spin constraints, and only then passes to pressure increments.

backbone: Explicit oracle circuit: rotate the target to a contracting block, encode it by truncated geometric-series Fourier fields, recurse on a smaller unitary, and compile everything into one Boolean oracle.
quote: For that purpose we construct two maps, $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal R$, from the original space into a register holding $Z$ together with a smaller state.

backbone: Reduce to type II_1; average a cocycle input over a constructed asymptotically free unitary random walk; a Liouville rigidity theorem turns the harmonic map into a bounded primitive.
quote: We obtain the needed module identity by averaging over a single unitary random walk.

backbone: Construct graphs of congruence fibers over discrete tori with a long collar; an integral class persists at every Rips scale, while maximal Roe-algebra transfer and rotation kill its index.
quote: We construct a graph with two torus ends and a long central region of constant fiber size.

backbone: Glue height-two local pieces via a complete operator with growing defects; a ghost/dual-detection criterion plus backward induction excludes every finite tower from BP<2>, while localizations still agree.
quote: For every sufficiently large prime $p$, we construct a connective $p$-complete spectrum $X$ of exact fp-type two outside the ordinary thick subcategory generated by the specified standard form of $\BP\langle2\rangle_p^\wedge$.

backbone: Define the dual of a segment-forest norm; verify reflexivity, a paired midpoint inequality, absence of equivalent AUC norms, and diamond distortion lower bounds via accumulated midpoint losses.
quote: We construct a separable reflexive real Banach space whose given norm is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex but which admits no asymptotically uniformly convex equivalent norm.

backbone: Necessity is easy; for sufficiency, split into three capacity cases and build packings via Kahler degenerations to normal models over curves, Moser transfer and a surface packing lemma.

backbone: Using Bamler-Kleiner tangent structure, a finite-jet obstruction yields a localized Lojasiewicz-type gradient inequality; iterative graph improvement and propagation with summable motion force convergence of rescalings.
quote: We now improve such graphs, propagate them for a fixed time, and sum the resulting motion with radii chosen from the preceding energy drops.

backbone: Assume a nonflat homogeneous minimizer in dimension at most six; an exactly verified algebraic certificate gives a test and flux field violating stability; a seven-dimensional example completes it.
quote: The extra positive mass $\epsilon_*w^{2a}$ will give the contradiction.
